Custom Print & Frame Builder — A UI/UX Case Study

Bring your work to life.

A solo, end-to-end interface for Fine Art Print Studio — a builder that walks an image from upload to a gallery-ready, archival framed print, with every material and every rupee in plain sight the whole way.

01 — The problem

A craft kept behind a counter.

Fine Art Print Studio does museum-grade work — true archival papers, custom framing, faithful reproduction. Yet the entire ordering ritual was offline: to commission a piece, you had to stand in the shop and choose materials by hand.

For a market this niche, that's a hard ceiling — the demand exists, the reach doesn't. The brief: lift it online without losing the one thing that earns trust in person — total visibility. Every paper, mount, frame, glass and fixing in the open, priced live, nothing hidden until checkout.

100% Pricing transparency, non-negotiable — the in-person promise, ported online. No demand could be reached while every order still required a physical visit.
02 — Act I · The storefront (shipped & live)

First, give the studio a front door.

Before the builder, the studio needed to exist online at all. The marketing site shipped first and is live now — a monochrome, sharp-cornered gallery that states the craft plainly and routes every visitor toward one action: start a print.

fineartprintstudios.inVisit live ↗
~5/wk
Qualified enquiries a week — inbound demand the studio never had before.
Global
Already fielding its first international print-shipping enquiry — reach well beyond the walk-in radius.

The front door works. The next problem: turning that inbound into finished orders — without a person behind the counter.

03 — The landscape

Builders existed.
Good ones didn't.

I tore down the few Indian print-and-frame builders that do exist — Wallvastra and Wallraft among them. The tools are there; the thinking isn't. Three gaps repeated, and together they drew the opening.

i

Out of order

The flow isn't linear. On one builder, the print & paper choice — the foundation of the whole piece — is asked at the very end, after the framing is already locked.

ii

Engineered, not designed

The experience reads as developer-built — confusing and unguided, with no sense that anyone shaped the journey. You assemble a product instead of being walked through one.

iii

No archival craft

None offer true archival-grade work — the exact thing the studio is known for. The premium tier of the market had no considered online home at all.

The thesis

A builder that is linear, obviously designed, and radically transparent — built around the craft.

04 — The build

Six steps,
one continuous decision.

A vertical icon rail anchors the journey from upload to fixings. Walk it left to right — each screen carries the call behind it.

01/
Upload & size
Drop a file, set units, dial exact dimensions and per-edge borders. Wall preview and spec panel populate at once — and Add to cart stays dark until the piece is real.
Drag-drop · units · borders · live preview
02/
Print & paper
The studio's signature, asked first — not last. Archival / Non-Archival, then real stocks named in the open: Felix-Schoeller, Hahnemühle — weight and price on the face.
Archival toggle · named stocks · gsm · protection
03/
Window mount
Mount-and-core pairings — white-on-white through black-on-white — each priced, sized to the edge. The mat redraws live, so the image-mount-frame relationship is watched, not imagined.
Core combos · per-edge sizing · live mat
04/
Framing & mounting
One switch for both finishing routes. Finish swatches across the top; below, Traditional Flat and Box profiles at honest, labelled widths down to the quarter-inch — the bench, on screen.
Flat / box · finish swatches · true widths
05/
Glass
Three grades — Standard, Anti-glare, Museum Grade — each in plain language about UV, reflection and clarity. The decision is framed around what you'll see, not a spec sheet.
Standard · anti-glare · museum grade
06/
Hanging material
The smallest, last call — D-hook or sawtooth — closes the loop. The spec sheet is complete, the cart goes live, and three room previews let the finished piece be checked in context.
D-hook / sawtooth · cart active · room previews
01 / 06
05 — Signature decisions

Three moves that
carry the trust.

01 / Preview

The live room mockup

The piece is staged on a real wall as it's built, alternate rooms a thumbnail away. Materials stop being a checklist and become an object you can picture owning.

02 / Ledger

Real-time price & spec

Printing, framing and total recompute on every choice; each selection writes into a running spec sheet. Full visibility, no hidden cost — the in-person promise, intact online.

03 / Path

A linear rail you can revisit

Steps run in the order a piece is genuinely made, while the icon rail reopens any decision without losing the rest. Complexity, made calm — the opposite of the teardown set.

i.

Let the work do the talking

A strictly black-and-white interface — silent chrome so the artwork carries every colour, the way galleries paint walls dark and light the canvas.

ii.

Sharp, every edge

Zero rounding, anywhere. Letter-spaced uppercase labels. A system precise enough to feel like the studio's own framing bench.

06 — Where it goes next

Built to be measured.

Act I is live and already pulling in enquiries the studio never had — including its first from overseas. Act II, the builder, is still in development, so its numbers are ahead of us. Here's what I'd watch once it ships.

  • →

    First-build completion. Can a newcomer go from upload to a finished, framed configuration without stalling? The linear rail is the bet.

  • →

    Drop-off vs the field. Whether paper-first sequencing and a linear flow lower abandonment against the non-linear builders mapped in discovery.

  • →

    Trust from transparency. Whether the always-visible ledger measurably lifts confidence and conversion on a high-consideration purchase.

  • →

    Mobile adaptation. Carrying the rail, live mockup and ledger into a single column without losing the sense of full visibility.

Monochrome.
Sharp-cornered. Built around the craft.
